l4_steps.name: Ingest WCHR/WCHC/WCHS/WCHB SSR codes from PNR
l4_steps.input: Passenger booking request or PNR with special assistance SSR codes
l4_steps.output: SSR codes attached to PNR and transmitted to ground handling agents via SITA Type B message
l4_steps.kpi: SSR capture rate ≥99% of passengers self-identifying as requiring assistance
l4_steps.pain_point: SSR codes entered via third-party OTA bookings (Sabre/Travelport GDS) frequently omit WCHR detail level — WCHR vs WCHC vs WCHB require different staffing and equipment, forcing manual re-verification at check-in

l4_steps.name: Validate SSR codes against IATA AIRIMP definitions
l4_steps.input: SSR codes from PNR (WCHR, WCHC, WCHB, WCHS, DEAF, BLND, UMNR)
l4_steps.output: Validated or corrected SSR categorisation confirmed in PNR
l4_steps.kpi: SSR validation accuracy ≥98% completed ≥24 hours before scheduled departure
l4_steps.pain_point: WCHR (ambulatory, needs chair to/from aircraft), WCHC (immobile), WCHB (on-board transfer only), WCHS (steps only) have distinct handling requirements — conflation causes resource misallocation and DOT ACAA exposure

l4_steps.name: Flag MEDA/OXYG/LEGL cases for medical clearance
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS + MedAire Medical Clearance Portal
l4_steps.input: SSR codes including MEDA (medical case), OXYG (oxygen), LEGL (stretcher), INCAD
l4_steps.output: Medical clearance decision or deferral notice attached to PNR
l4_steps.kpi: Medical clearance decision issued ≤4 hours before departure; MEDA clearance rate tracked monthly
l4_steps.pain_point: MEDA cases require physician sign-off via MedAire or equivalent — no standardised PSS-to-medical portal API; clearance requests are manual email/phone, creating decision latency that can strand medically complex passengers

l4_steps.name: Generate special assistance manifest for flight
l4_steps.input: Finalised SSR list pushed from Amadeus Altéa PSS, flight departure schedule
l4_steps.output: Special assistance manifest: pax count by category, seat numbers, mobility device details
l4_steps.kpi: Manifest accuracy ≥97% verified at gate against actual presenting passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time SSR updates from late bookers and day-of upgrades are not always pushed from Altéa to SITA AMS — agents frequently work off stale manifests, missing newly added WCHR requests

l4_steps.name: Allocate wheelchair equipment and trained staff
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + Workforce Management System (Jeppesen Crew Management)
l4_steps.input: Special assistance manifest, available equipment inventory, staff roster
l4_steps.output: Staff assignments confirmed, wheelchair and aisle chair allocation per flight logged in AMS
l4_steps.kpi: WCHR equipment availability ≥99.5% at departure time; staff-to-WCHR ratio ≥1:3
l4_steps.pain_point: Shared wheelchair pool across concurrent bank departures causes equipment shortfalls — no real-time IoT tracking of wheelchair/aisle chair location at most airports; agents spend 10–15 min locating equipment

l4_steps.name: Brief check-in, gate, and lounge staff on SSR pax
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + Airline Ops Communication App
l4_steps.input: Staff duty roster, special assistance manifest, gate assignments
l4_steps.output: Pre-departure briefing confirmed, staff aware of individual passenger needs and mobility restrictions
l4_steps.kpi: Briefing completion ≥90 minutes before scheduled departure for all WCHR flights
l4_steps.pain_point: High turnover in ground handling contractor staff means briefings are the primary knowledge transfer channel — no structured digital briefing delivery to ramp contractor teams; verbal-only handoffs cause information loss at shift changes

l4_steps.name: Meet and greet passenger at curbside or check-in
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Passenger arrival at airport, WCHR manifest from Phase 2
l4_steps.output: Passenger confirmed on manifest, escort service initiated and logged in AMS
l4_steps.kpi: Meet-and-greet wait time ≤5 minutes from passenger arrival notification; missed meet rate <1%
l4_steps.pain_point: No reliable mechanism for passengers to pre-notify airport of their actual arrival time — agents use scheduled departure window as proxy, causing missed meets for passengers arriving >90 min early or late

l4_steps.name: Process priority check-in and accessible seat assignment
l4_steps.input: PNR, validated SSR category, mobility device dimensions and weight
l4_steps.output: Boarding pass issued, bulkhead or aisle seat assigned, mobility device tagged for gate-check or cargo
l4_steps.kpi: Priority check-in processing time ≤10 minutes; accessible seat assignment compliance ≥100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa seat maps do not surface DOT Part 382-mandated accessible seats (bulkhead with movable armrests) separately from general inventory — agents must manually cross-check airline accessible seating policy to avoid assigning window or obstructed seats

l4_steps.name: Escort passenger through security checkpoint
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + TSA PreCheck / Airport Security System
l4_steps.input: Boarding pass, passenger with personal mobility device
l4_steps.output: Passenger cleared through security, mobility device screened and returned, security escort time logged
l4_steps.kpi: Security escort completion ≤20 minutes; extended screening incidents <5% of WCHR escorts
l4_steps.pain_point: TSA screening of power wheelchairs with lithium batteries (>300Wh) triggers extended secondary screening — no pre-clearance pathway between airline SSR data and TSA PreCheck; battery removal for screening adds 15–20 minutes and requires specialised TSA training

l4_steps.name: Pre-board WCHR passengers ahead of general boarding
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS (boarding control) + SITA Airport Management System (AMS)
l4_steps.input: WCHR manifest, gate assignment, boarding gate opening time
l4_steps.output: WCHR passengers boarded before general boarding commences, boarding scan logged in Altéa
l4_steps.kpi: Pre-boarding initiation ≥20 minutes before scheduled departure; WCHR pre-board completion rate ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Gate changes issued via Amadeus AMS real-time updates do not automatically trigger re-dispatch of staged WCHR escort teams — agents must manually monitor FIDS for gate swaps, causing missed pre-boards when late gate changes occur

l4_steps.name: Transfer passenger to aisle chair at jet bridge threshold
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + Airline Aisle Chair Inventory System
l4_steps.input: WCHC or WCHB passenger at gate, aisle chair staged at jet bridge
l4_steps.output: Passenger safely transferred to aisle chair and escorted to assigned seat
l4_steps.kpi: Aisle chair transfer completion ≤8 minutes per passenger; transfer injury rate 0%
l4_steps.pain_point: Narrow-body aircraft (737, A320 family) require airline-specific aisle chair dimensions — third-party ground handling company equipment is frequently incompatible; DOT Air Carrier Access Act mandates two trained staff for transfers, but solo escorts are common at smaller stations

l4_steps.name: Tag, stow, or gate-check personal mobility device
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS (baggage tagging) + SITA Baggage Reconciliation System (BRS)
l4_steps.input: Personal wheelchair, power scooter, or walker; baggage tag from check-in
l4_steps.output: Mobility device tagged, stowed gate-check or in cargo hold, recorded in SITA BRS with return location flag
l4_steps.kpi: Mobility device stow without damage ≥99.8%; aircraft-door return ≥90% of WCHC/WCHB cases
l4_steps.pain_point: Power wheelchair lithium batteries >300Wh require IATA DGR Section 3.3.1 special handling — ramp agents are not universally IATA DGR certified; battery removal adds 15–20 min dwell time and risks damage to chair electronics if improperly handled

l4_steps.name: Confirm seating, call bell, and lavatory access briefing
l4_steps.system: Aircraft Cabin Systems (IFE / Seat Control) + SITA Airport Management System (AMS)
l4_steps.input: Passenger seated, boarding in progress, pre-departure checklist
l4_steps.output: Passenger briefed on accessible IFE, call bell, and lavatory access; assistance closure logged in AMS
l4_steps.kpi: Passenger safety and accessibility briefing completion 100% before door close
l4_steps.pain_point: Single-aisle narrow-body aircraft (737-800, A320) have no onboard accessible lavatory — WCHR passengers on sectors >3 hours require a pre-departure lavatory visit; this is frequently omitted when boarding is behind schedule, resulting in DOT ACAA complaints

l4_steps.name: Transmit WCHR count and SSR detail to destination station
l4_steps.system: SITA Messaging (Type B / IATA AHM) + Amadeus Altéa PSS (SSR relay)
l4_steps.input: SSR manifest, confirmed pax list, flight ETA
l4_steps.output: LDM/PSM/IATA AHM 140 PRM advice message transmitted to destination with WCHR count and categories
l4_steps.kpi: SSR transmission to destination ≥60 minutes before ETA; message accuracy ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Not all carriers use structured IATA AHM 140 (PRM advice) messaging — some destination stations rely on informal teletype or email, causing missed meet-and-greets at remote or outstations with minimal ground handling staff

l4_steps.name: Deplane WCHR passengers in coordinated sequence
l4_steps.role: Cabin Crew + Arrival Special Assistance Agent
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Aircraft at blocks-on, WCHR manifest from arrival station, aisle chair staged at jet bridge
l4_steps.output: WCHR passengers deplaned safely, arrival assistance confirmed and logged in SITA AMS
l4_steps.kpi: WCHR deplaning completion within 15 minutes of blocks-on; missed assist rate <0.5% of WCHR arrivals
l4_steps.pain_point: Remote stands (bus gates) require two-stage transfer: aisle chair → ambulift → terminal wheelchair — ambulift availability is not tracked in SITA AMS; unplanned remote stand assignments cause 20–30 min assistance delays and DOT ACAA complaint exposure

l4_steps.name: Return mobility device at aircraft door or baggage claim
l4_steps.system: SITA Baggage Reconciliation System (BRS) + SITA Airport Management System (AMS)
l4_steps.input: Tagged mobility device retrieved from cargo hold, arrival WCHR manifest
l4_steps.output: Device returned to passenger in original condition; damage inspection completed and logged
l4_steps.kpi: Device return at aircraft door ≥90% (DOT ACAA requirement); mobility device damage rate <0.1 per 1,000 devices handled
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT Air Carrier Access Act requires power wheelchair return at aircraft door — carriers routinely return at baggage claim due to cargo door sequencing constraints; each violation exposes the carrier to DOT fines of up to $35,000 per incident

l4_steps.name: Log completed assistance events in SITA AMS
l4_steps.input: Assistance completion confirmations from agents, timestamps, staff IDs
l4_steps.output: Digital event log of WCHR assistance with timestamps, pax IDs, staff IDs, and outcomes
l4_steps.kpi: Assistance event logging rate ≥99% within 30 minutes of flight departure or arrival blocks-on
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual data entry creates compliance gaps — paper-based backup processes at smaller outstations mean event logs are incomplete; data aggregation for monthly DOT Part 382 reporting requires manual reconciliation across 8–12 station formats

l4_steps.name: Audit DOT Part 382 / ACAA compliance metrics
l4_steps.system: Tableau / Power BI (Compliance Dashboard) + SITA AMS Data Export
l4_steps.input: Assistance event logs, complaint records, mobility device damage and delay reports
l4_steps.output: Monthly DOT Part 382 compliance scorecard, gap analysis, corrective action register
l4_steps.kpi: DOT ACAA complaint rate <0.5 per 10,000 passengers; mobility device damage claims <0.1%; complaint resolution within 30 days ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT Part 382 requires individual written complaint response within 30 days — complaint tracking spans CX, legal, and ground ops with no single integrated system; manual status reconciliation between Salesforce CRM and SITA AMS takes 2–3 hours per month per station

l4_steps.name: Escalate unresolved complaints to CX and Regulatory Affairs
l4_steps.role: Customer Experience Manager / Regulatory Affairs Director
l4_steps.system: Salesforce Service Cloud (CRM) + SITA Airport Management System (AMS)
l4_steps.input: Open DOT/ACAA complaints, device damage claims, missed assist incident reports
l4_steps.output: Escalation ticket created in Salesforce, root cause analysis completed, process improvement recommendation issued
l4_steps.kpi: Complaint resolution within 30 days ≥95% (DOT Part 382 §382.155 requirement); repeat incident rate reduction target ≥20% quarter-over-quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: No direct integration between SITA AMS ground ops incident logs and Salesforce CRM — staff must manually recreate incident context in Salesforce tickets, causing information loss and duplicate investigative effort; recurring root causes (e.g. remote stand ambulift gaps) are not systematically fed back into resource planning
